messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — high error rate for tenant acme-corp on Dedicated pool (us-west-2 VPC). 5m 5xx rate rose from ~12% to 45%. KV/prefix cache global hit-rate for this tenant collapsed from 95% -> 2%. Creating thread for coordination. Please ack and assign.

emma: acked. I'm on-call. tagging @jon for infra help and @priya for model/runtime context.

jon: seeing same in metrics dashboard — eviction rate for cache backend spiked, memstore CPU at 78%. Looks like cache keys exploded for tenant prefixes. Any recent customer-side churn? @customer-eng can you weigh in?

customer-eng: acme-corp pushed a release ~50m ago that added dynamic user prefixes for search suggestions. They reported higher QPS but no errors on their side. They allowed arbitrary prefixes so that could explain key cardinality growth.

priya: if prefix cardinality jumped, prefix/KV cache will be polluted (low reuse). Two quick mitigations: 1) flip tenant-level cache flag to disabled (stop populating/reading prefix cache) — fast and low risk; 2) route acme traffic to fallback non-cached model variant (higher token cost but avoids cache pressure).

michael: I can flip the tenant cache flag. Command (internal API):

```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.local/tenants/acme-corp/cache -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"enabled": false}'
```

Note: this disables prefix caching only for acme-corp; other tenants unaffected.

olga: recommend evicting the current tenant namespace keys to free memory too. I can run a targeted eviction job after flag flip. Eviction command: `redis-cli --scan --pattern "acme:*" | xargs redis-cli del` (will throttle deletes).

emma: plan: 1) michael flips tenant cache -> disabled. 2) olga starts phased eviction (rate-limited). 3) priya will route 10% -> non-cached model initially to validate. 4) monitor error rate and latency; escalate to pool drain if errors persist.

jon: note — draining dedicated pool will require moving live sessions; we should avoid unless necessary. Also ensure we don't accidentally disable global caching. Confirming: michael will execute only tenant-scoped API.

michael: executing now. POST returned 202 accepted. Cache flag for acme-corp set to false.

sre-bot: automation note — cache-flag-change event recorded: event_id=evt_3487. Added to incident log.

olga: starting eviction job with 5k keys/min throttle. I'll report progress every 5 minutes.

priya: rolling 10% traffic -> non-cached variant (variant-id: model-v2-nocache) using routing policy: `route.set_weight(tenant='acme-corp', variant='model-v2-nocache', weight=10)`

emma: seeing immediate improvement in 5xx now down to 18% within 4m of flag flip. Latency up ~40ms average for affected requests. Hit-rate metric slowly rising for non-prefixed caches (expected).

jon: memstore CPU trending down to 45%. Eviction rate leveling. Good sign.

customer-eng: told Acme support we disabled tenant prefix cache and are evicting stale keys; they confirmed their deployment will be reverted if it causes issues. They asked for ETA — please add a short customer-facing summary once stabilized.

michael: eviction job completed ~38k keys removed. No errors in the delete job logs.

olga: final metrics — tenant cache hit-rate now reported as N/A (disabled) while non-cached variant hit metrics show expected higher model cost but stable latency. 5xx back near baseline (6%).

emma: moving incident state to mitigation: temporary tenant cache disable + eviction + partial traffic shift. Root cause likely prefix cardinality explosion due to customer-side dynamic prefixes. Follow-ups: 1) add tenant quota/alerts on cache key cardinality, 2) provide guidance to customers about prefix cardinality, 3) add automatic fallback routing when tenant-level cache hit-rate collapses.

priya: I'll open a post-incident action item for model/runtime tweaks and a retro doc with suggested SDK/usage guidance for customers.

emma: handing off to @jon for overnight watch. Jon, please escalate to platform oncall if error rate creeps above 15% or latency > 1s for >5m.

jon: taking over. I'll keep an eye and update channel every hour.

sre-bot: incident summary recorded. Severity: Sev2 (customer-impacting, mitigated). Follow-up ticket: INF-4721.

emma: thanks team. I'll prepare the customer-facing incident note and tag the account team. :white_check_mark:
